evidence.decision: Argentine Republic is an official constitutional name of the same Argentine state represented canonically as Argentina, not a separate sovereign identity. Argentine Constitution Article 35 recognizes República Argentina among the official names of the government and territory, and Argentina.gob.ar records that President Santiago Derqui standardized República Argentina for administrative acts on 8 October 1860. The already-applied continuity correction relinked Domingo Faustino Sarmiento's 1868-1874 presidency to canonical Argentina without inventing a closed temporal-name phase.
